question: Why do pregnant women often develop physiological anaemia?

options.A: Rapid destruction of red blood cells by the placenta
options.B: Severe dietary protein deficiency in early pregnancy
options.C: The bone marrow completely stops making new blood cells
options.D: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cells

explanation: You've got this! Think of it like adding more water to juice: the red blood cells are still there, but the fluid (plasma) increases so much that it gets diluted. This is completely normal in pregnancy! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h1)

question: Why does the body increase blood volume so massively during pregnancy?

options.A: To store extra calcium needed for the baby's developing bones
options.B: To increase the physical strength of the maternal heart muscle
options.C: To provide extra fluid protection against blood loss during delivery
options.D: To completely prevent the mother from ever catching infections

explanation: Nature is amazing! The extra blood acts as a safety cushion for the blood loss that naturally happens when giving birth. Brilliant design, right? [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h1)

question: Which hormone tells the bone marrow to make more red blood cells during pregnancy?
explanation: Erythropoietin is like a special chemical messenger released by the kidneys to tell the bone marrow, 'Hey, we need more red blood cells for the baby!' [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks is tired, and tests show true iron deficiency. Where did most of her missing iron go?

options.A: Stored permanently inside the maternal liver cells
options.B: To the developing fetus and the placenta
options.C: Excreted rapidly through the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Lost entirely through excessive maternal sweating

explanation: The growing baby always gets first priority! The baby and placenta draw a lot of iron from the mother to build their own systems. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h2)

question: During a normal pregnancy, which white blood cell type increases the most?
explanation: Neutrophils are the troops that rise the most during pregnancy to help keep the mother's immune system ready. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h3)

question: Why must nurses know that a normal pregnant woman can have a high white blood cell count?

options.A: To determine the correct dose of routine iron supplements
options.B: To avoid misinterpreting a normal pregnancy change as a severe infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date when spontaneous labour will begin
options.D: To prove that the mother's immune system is completely shut down

explanation: Good nursing judgment! Knowing what is normal for pregnancy prevents us from panicking or treating a healthy mum for an infection she doesn't have. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h3)

question: What is the main danger of the clotting-heavy state (hypercoagulability) seen in pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden and severe drop in total white blood cell count
options.B: Permanent destruction of all circulating platelets
options.C: Inability of the blood to form any scabs after a cut
options.D: Increased risk of unwanted blood clots in the veins

explanation: The body gets ready to prevent heavy bleeding after birth, but this downside means blood can form dangerous clots in the legs too easily. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h4)

question: Which clotting protein increases a lot during pregnancy to prepare for childbirth?
explanation: Fibrinogen is a key player in blood clotting. It rises nicely during pregnancy to protect the mother from heavy bleeding during delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h4)

question: What happens to the white blood cell count during active labour and delivery?

options.A: It surges even higher due to physical stress and tissue trauma
options.B: It drops rapidly to near-zero levels to protect the baby
options.C: It remains completely unchanged throughout the entire process
options.D: It fluctuates wildly based on the mother's blood type

explanation: Labour is hard work! The physical stress causes the white blood cell count to jump up even more right around delivery time. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h5)

question: Why does a healthy woman usually handle the blood loss of childbirth without going into shock?

options.A: Her platelet count drops to zero to prevent any fluid movement
options.B: Her total blood volume expanded significantly during pregnancy
options.C: Her bone marrow stops all red blood cell production temporarily
options.D: Her heart rate drops to zero during every single uterine contraction

explanation: Remember all that extra volume she built up over nine months? It acts as a safety buffer so she handles delivery blood loss like a champ. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h5)

question: How does a new mother's body mainly get rid of extra pregnancy fluids right after birth?

options.A: Through increased production of bile acids
options.B: Through reabsorption into the bone marrow
options.D: Through rapid shedding of stomach lining

explanation: Peeing and sweating a lot in the first few days postpartum is totally normal—it's just the body's way of flushing out the extra pregnancy fluids! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h6)

question: A nursing mother is three weeks postpartum and resting in bed. Why is she still at risk for a blood clot (deep vein thrombosis)?

options.A: Her white blood cell count remains elevated due to breastfeeding
options.B: Her plasma volume expands even further during the fourth week
options.C: Her red blood cell count instantly drops to zero after childbirth
options.D: The hypercoagulable state of pregnancy lingers for several weeks

explanation: Even after birth, the body's clotting system takes a few weeks to settle back to normal, which is why we must keep a close eye on new mums. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h6)

question: Why do nurses encourage new mothers to walk around soon after delivery (early ambulation)?

options.A: To completely eliminate white blood cells from circulation
options.B: To stimulate the kidneys to stop producing erythropoietin
options.C: To help prevent dangerous blood clots in the deep veins
options.D: To immediately restore the pre-pregnancy plasma volume

explanation: Get those legs moving! Walking helps blood circulate properly and stops clots from forming in the legs after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)

question: What is the best nursing action when caring for a pregnant woman with physiological anaemia?

options.A: Administer large doses of intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.B: Provide education on taking routine iron and folate supplements
options.C: Advise the patient to stop drinking water to thicken her blood
options.D: Prepare the patient for an emergency blood transfusion today

explanation: Routine antenatal iron and folate are key! As a nurse, teaching the mum how to take her supplements correctly makes all the difference. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)
